messages:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty SEV2 triggered: streaming-api > elevated 5xx and disconnects (auto-assigned to Rachel (oncall)) :rotating_light:
Rachel (oncall): I'm on it. Hemant, any customer reports?
Hemant (support): Yes — 3 customers reported streaming disconnects and partial responses since ~10:03 UTC. All via the /v1/stream endpoint. Example from logs: `client: 54.36.12.7 - err: 'client canceled'`
Rachel (oncall): Thanks. Jordan can you pull the realtime error rate?
Jordan (sre): looking... stackdriver shows streaming-api 5xx spike starting 10:02 -> peak at 10:07. 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% -> 7.8% for streaming routes. p99 latency also up from 1.1s -> 5.6s.
Matt (runtime): I'm seeing a lot of downstream `write` errors in host-agent logs: `writev: broken pipe` and `failed to send chunk: connection reset by peer`. Many look like clients cancelling mid-stream.
Caroline (ingest): Fanout count increased for some requests (avg fanout per request 1.9 -> 3.7). A few large prompt customers triggered multi-target fanout. Could be amplifying the problem.
Rachel (oncall): Quick mitigation options? Prioritize low-risk, fast rollouts.
Jordan (sre): Immediate: 1) enable streaming->paged fallback for affected routes (drop chunked transfer and return paged responses) 2) throttle heavy fanout clients by UA 3) move traffic to dedicated infra pool if capacity shows errors are region-specific.
Matt (runtime): I can flip the streaming fallback toggle for the route group `customer-facing/stream` now — this forces non-chunked paged responses for existing sessions. Low config risk.
Rachel (oncall): Do it. Post the command and I'll ack.
Matt (runtime): Running:
```
# toggle fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane/api/toggles/streaming_fallback -d '{"route":"customer-facing/stream","enabled":true}'
```
Matt (runtime): Toggle confirmed. Rolling out to prod tier-2.
Ops-bot: Deploy job queued: rollout/toggle/streaming_fallback -> started on 6 nodes
Jordan (sre): Throttle rule in wg: `if user_agent in heavy_clients and requests_last_min > 200 then rate_limit=10rps` — pushing now.
Ops-bot: Rate-limit policy applied to route group `customer-facing/stream` for tag `heavy_clients`.
Hemant (support): Early customer check: one of the impacted customers reports immediate improvement on their end (they were seeing disconnects every 10s, now stable).
Rachel (oncall): Good. Monitor 5xx and p99. Jordan share graphs.
Jordan (sre): Live: 5xx dropping from 7.8% -> 2.1% over last 4 minutes. p99 latency down to ~2.1s. Still above baseline but trending down.
Maya (eng): I'm seeing a subset of backend hosts (ip range 10.45.12.*) with repeated epoll/kqueue errors after a kernel update earlier today. dmesg shows: `epoll_wait returned -1 errno=EFAULT` on a few nodes. Could be causing socket resets during chunked transfers.
Matt (runtime): That aligns: chunked transfer requires continuous writev, and an epoll regression could cause in-flight connections to drop. If true then fallback to paged responses avoids long-lived write churn.
Rachel (oncall): If kernel regression is likely, we should isolate those hosts and spin up replacements. Ryan from Infra?
Infra (ryan): I'm isolating the suspect pool. Starting drain of 4 nodes in us-west-2a with `kernel-5.14.8` -> requeue to allow autoscaler to replace.
Paul (customer-ops): Heads-up: one enterprise customer wants a carrier-level update. I'll prepare a short note if we can confirm mitigation and ETA for full fix.
Jordan (sre): Quick debug output from nginx upstream logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T10:05:14Z upstream: 504, upstream_response_time: 0.12, request_time: 12.04, client: 54.36.12.7
2026-03-15T10:05:15Z upstream: 502, error: "recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)", backend: 10.45.12.21
```
Jordan (sre): Note the request_time ~12s — long-lived. Many of these are chunked streaming sessions that ended in backend resets.
Caroline (ingest): We also saw proto-level `chunked-trailer-mismatch` logs (rarely before) spike times 38x. Could be trailing chunk corruption if a socket reset occurs during trailer write.
Rachel (oncall): Good catch. For now fallback is live and 5xx reduced. Next steps: infra to remediate hosts, runtime to prepare canary rollback of kernel or repro on staging.
Infra (ryan): Drains started. Replacements queued: template `r-inference-5.13` spin-up -> expected healthy in 8-10m.
Matt (runtime): Also pushing a temporary workaround in runtime to increase socket write retries and extend keepalive slightly (from 30s -> 60s) to help flaky nets. Deploying a small hotfix to staging then prod.
Ops-bot: Hotfix rollout `runtime/soft-retry-write` started (canary 2 nodes).
Maya (eng): I'm capturing tcpdump traces from one affected host for further offline analysis. Will paste a sample if useful.
Rachel (oncall): Hemant loop in customers that reported impact with status: mitigation applied (fallback) and we're monitoring. Paul, please send concise customer note.
Paul (customer-ops): Draft:
"We experienced elevated streaming disconnects impacting a subset of streaming sessions. We applied a temporary fallback to paged responses which reduced errors. Engineering is isolating affected hosts and preparing a full remediation. We will follow up with root cause and ETA for a permanent fix."
Paul (customer-ops): sending now.
Hemant (support): Affected customers acknowledged and appreciate the quick workaround. They asked about retries behavior on client side — recommended to implement exponential backoff + idempotency keys for paged resumes.
Jordan (sre): Monitoring: 5xx now ~0.9% and trending to baseline. No new PagerDuty escalations in last 6 minutes.
Rachel (oncall): Once infra confirms replacement healthy, we should re-enable streaming on a small % of traffic (canary) to validate kernel fix. Matt coordinate the canary.
Matt (runtime): Will do. Canary plan: enable streaming for 2% traffic routed to new hosts only, watch p99 and 5xx for 15m. If stable, ramp.
Infra (ryan): New nodes healthy at 10:24 UTC. Rotating 4 drained nodes out of service.
Ops-bot: Canary traffic rule applied: route 2% to hosts with tag `kernel-5.13`.
Maya (eng): Early canary telemetry: no connection resets, chunked trailers look correct.
Jordan (sre): 15m post-canary: rolling forward. 5xx stable ~0.2%, p99 ~1.2s.
Rachel (oncall): Great. Prepare postmortem notes: timelines, mitigation (fallback toggle, rate-limit), root cause hypothesis (kernel/epoll regression causing socket resets under chunked write), and action items: kernel rollback verification, add host-level epoll error alert, add client guidance for resume/retries.
Paul (customer-ops): I'll follow up with customers with full postmortem once engineering confirms root cause.
Infra (ryan): I'll file infra ticket INFRA-2026 to track kernel audit and host remediation.
Matt (runtime): I'll file RUNTIME-2026 for adding a defensive `chunked-fallback` heuristic in runtime (auto-fallback if backend reset rate > X within Y minutes).
Rachel (oncall): Handoff to infra/runtime for remediation. I'll mark the incident as mitigated but keep the channel open until root cause confirmed. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
incidents-bot: Incident SEV2 status changed to MITIGATED by Rachel (oncall) at 10:32 UTC
Rachel (oncall): handing to Infra and Runtime for post-incident. Using this thread as the handoff.
Infra (ryan): acknowledged, taking ownership for follow-up.
Matt (runtime): acknowledged, taking runtime follow-up.
Hemant (support): closing customer tickets as 'monitoring' for now, will reopen if recurring.
Rachel (oncall): I'll start the brief before-postmortem doc and assign owners. Closing live coordination phase.
